title: AHB Address and Control Signals
description: Select a master-driven signal to see its direction, sampling rule, important values, and the bug a monitor should catch.

signals.name: HADDR
signals.description: Identifies the byte address targeted by the transfer.
signals.sampled: Rising HCLK edge when HREADY is HIGH; held stable while HREADY is LOW
signals.verificationNote: Flag misalignment and any address change during a wait state.

signals.name: HWRITE
signals.description: Selects write data from the master or read data from the slave.
signals.verificationNote: Must remain consistent for every beat of a burst.

signals.name: HSIZE
signals.description: Encodes the payload size of each transfer beat and therefore the address increment.
signals.verificationNote: Check data-bus width limits and HADDR alignment.

signals.name: HBURST
signals.description: Declares whether the transfer is single, incrementing, or wrapping and gives fixed beat count where applicable.
signals.sampled: At the first beat and stable across the burst
signals.verificationNote: A mid-burst HBURST change is a protocol violation.

signals.name: HTRANS
signals.description: Tells the slave whether the current address phase is idle, busy, a new transfer, or a continuing burst beat.
signals.sampled: Rising HCLK edge when HREADY is HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Only NONSEQ and SEQ indicate valid transfers; a burst must start with NONSEQ.

signals.name: HPROT
signals.description: Describes instruction/data, user/privileged, bufferable, and cacheable properties for access control and memory behavior.
signals.verificationNote: Verify protected slaves reject disallowed attributes with the intended response.

signals.name: HMASTLOCK
signals.description: Marks a sequence that must retain ownership in a multi-master context.
signals.sampled: With the address phase for the locked sequence
signals.verificationNote: Check lock begins and ends at legal transfer boundaries and cannot starve other masters indefinitely.
